reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the Parameters StructureDefinition findings, the direct behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `Parameters`, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings only as background. I checked the deterministic aggregate after forming the resource-level judgment rather than using counts as the decision rule.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Parameters is normative and FMM 5, so hard validation breaks and generic operation-envelope behavior changes need strong justification. That pressure is somewhat tempered for changes that merely track the R6 datatype inventory, but it is not tempered for low-cost transition behavior around operation response envelopes.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Parameters keeps its identity and model shape, but targeted migration is needed for operation envelopes and `value[x]` choice changes; low-cost compatibility preservation still has high value.

reasoning.thesisMd: `Parameters` is not removed or broadly remodeled in R6. The local resource shape is largely intact, but the one hard forward break (`valueContributor`) and the direct operation-envelope behavior changes mean implementers cannot treat R4-to-R6 Parameters handling as purely mechanical. Because the R4 resource is normative/FMM 5, the presence of some necessary migration does not make additional avoidable breaks unimportant.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions retain the same resource identity, specialization from `Resource`, element count, cardinalities, and core `parameter`/`part` recursion. The substantive local model change is the `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` type domain: R6 removes `Contributor` and adds `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`. That creates a targeted choice-type/API/validation migration, not a whole-resource remodel.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Migration is only partial and targeted, so compatibility leverage remains strong. The generic operation response-envelope change is especially avoidable-looking: allowing both the R4 `Parameters` wrapper and the direct resource form would preserve mature operation clients while still enabling the simpler R6 response style. The `valueContributor` break is less attractive to preserve because it would require retaining an otherwise removed datatype in the R6 base datatype surface.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The best low-cost alternative is for operation responses with a single resource return: keep the R4 wrapper as an allowed transition form while preferring direct resources. A partial alternative also exists for `$care-gaps`, allowing the R4 direct `Bundle` for exactly-one-result cases while using `Parameters` for zero or multiple returns. By contrast, retaining `valueContributor` is not low-cost because it depends on preserving the removed `Contributor` datatype, and suppressing new R6 `value[x]` datatypes would undercut Parameters as a generic R6 operation carrier.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: Direct behavior changes matter more than the local prose findings. The generic HTTP operation-envelope rule affects Parameters in its central role as the operation input/output wrapper and deserves standards review. The `$care-gaps` response-envelope change is a high runtime break but is operation-specific and belongs primarily to Measure/quality-measure migration planning. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because Parameters is not the base `Resource` or `DomainResource` artifact under review.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I broadly agree with the aggregate's `Partial` migration conclusion and `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks` shape. My emphasis is that the resource has not crossed into migration-program-dominates territory: the remaining compatibility work should be judged per change, with strong pressure to preserve low-cost operation-envelope compatibility even though targeted migration is already likely.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The computable StructureDefinition evidence is clear. The main uncertainty is standards intent: the local packages do not provide detailed ballot rationale for removing `Contributor` from the datatype inventory or for making some operation response-envelope changes mandatory.

findingConsiderations.title: Parameters.parameter.value[x] no longer accepts Contributor
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only local hard old-valid/new-invalid instance break: an R4 `valueContributor` branch is not in the R6 `value[x]` type list. It drives the conclusion that some targeted choice-type migration is real, but it is not enough to make a wholesale Parameters migration unavoidable because apparent core-operation prevalence is narrow and preservation would require retaining the removed `Contributor` datatype.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds six Parameters.parameter.value[x] datatypes with no R4 counterpart
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not a forward R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is important for cross-version gateways and generated SDKs because R6 can emit `valueInteger64`, `valueCodeableReference`, and other choice names that R4 cannot parse. It is a local migration chore once R6 datatype support is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 removes the R4 comment limiting nested Parameters.parameter.part to one level
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The computable recursive structure remains; no depth-limiting invariant was removed. This may require local policy checks for systems that enforced the old comment, but it does not materially change the resource-level migration posture.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 text explicitly allows additional resources in Parameters.parameter.resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element remains `Resource` with the same cardinality. Unknown additional resource types can break R4 parsers in reverse-version exchange, but that is not a local forward Parameters model break.

findingConsiderations.title: Operation responses with a single resource return changed from optional unwrapping to required unwrapping
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most standards-review-worthy Parameters-related issue. It changes the generic operation wire shape from allowing a `Parameters` wrapper to requiring an unwrapped resource in a common pattern. A less-breaking design allowing both forms looks comparatively low cost for a normative operation framework.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 changes successful responses from a direct Bundle to Parameters containing repeated return Bundles
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a high runtime break for `$care-gaps` clients because the top-level response changes from `Bundle` to `Parameters`, but it is an operation-specific redesign rather than evidence that the Parameters resource model is broadly remodeled. A single-result compatibility mode is worth considering.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This representative shared behavior finding was considered only as background. Its affected resources do not include Parameters directly, and the review rubric says shared Resource/DomainResource behavior should not be scored for every resource.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the generic operation response-envelope rule and consider retaining the R4 `Parameters` wrapper as an allowed transition form for single-resource `return` responses while preferring direct resources in R6.

Publish explicit migration guidance for `Parameters.parameter.value[x]`: how to handle removed `Contributor`, and how cross-version gateways should map or reject new R6 choices such as `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, and `Availability`.

For `$care-gaps`, decide whether R6 can preserve a direct `Bundle` response for exactly-one-result compatibility, or document the mandatory `Parameters` envelope break and negotiation expectations clearly.
Treat the `part` nesting and additional-resource prose changes as documentation/parser-compatibility guidance rather than drivers of resource-level redesign.

caveats: Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were not scored for Parameters unless they directly named Parameters.
The review uses local package StructureDefinitions and reports; official ballot rationale for the underlying design choices was not available in the supplied inputs.
The `$care-gaps` behavior finding affects Parameters as an envelope type, but its domain migration belongs primarily with the Measure operation.
